title: Brig. Gen. C. C. Augur (Dept of Texas) to Lt Gen Sheridan and Maj. G. B. Russell: three 'Cypher' telegrams during the Texas gubernatorial crisis (Davis/Coke), Jan 1874
correspondents: C. C. Augur to P. H. Sheridan (Chicago); Augur to G. B. Russell (Austin)
place: San Antonio, Texas (HQ Department of Texas)
shelfmark: Newberry Library, Ayer MS 3008 (Christopher C. Augur papers, letter-books of the Departments of Texas and the Gulf), box 02, scan 00045-1; telegram nos. 8529 and following
folio_note: one scan page with three telegrams of about 50-60 words each, copied as scrambled English words (word transposition, with 'Cypher' left as a stray word); more cipher telegrams may sit elsewhere in the 1873-74 letter-books
status: Newberry's volunteer transcription (Newberry Transcribe) types the three telegrams as scrambled word strings, e.g. 'Dresden I persons to it fussy unauthorized forward ... Cypher state Grant ...'; no plaintext is given. The 18 Feb 1869 letter in Ayer MS 3039 (Grierson papers, box 03 f.153) describes the army cypher method then used in Texas: write the message in 4 to 9 columns, a key sets the reading order, key words are substituted. Not checked on DECODE beyond known.py (no hit for Augur cipher). Scan viewed 29 Oct 2026 (collections.newberry.org, Image w/ Text): letter-book page 31 with telegrams 8529 (to Sheridan, 12 Jan 1874), 30 and 45 (to Russell, 12 and 17 Jan 1874) in clerk's hand as scrambled English words with code words (Dresden, Cheyenne, Neces, Houston, Waco); no decipherment on the page.
why: Augur's private cipher traffic with Sheridan during the Jan 1874 Texas political crisis (Governor Davis refusing to yield to Coke) would show what the army told Washington; also a clean test of a US Army word-transposition cipher with a described key.
score_note: Scored during the Oct 2026 Chicago Collections Consortium sweep (research/chi_consortium/); scan viewed 29 Oct 2026 in Newberry Digital Collections
verify: Open the scan (collections.newberry.org asset 2KXJ8ZSFQY9EQ) and check the ciphertext is the scrambled words and not a decipherment printed in cipher order; read the 18 Feb 1869 key letter (Ayer MS 3039 box 03 f.153, asset 2KXJ8ZSC7CU0W) and its second page for the column-order rule; try 4-9 column transpositions with nulls.
prior_art: open (checked 29 Oct 2026: web search for Augur 1874 cipher telegram and Fifth Military District cipher found nothing; cryptiana, HistoCrypt and Lasry not searched for US Army 1869-74 ciphers)
access_note: scans online, free, at Newberry Digital Collections (collections.newberry.org); volunteer transcription at nt.newberry.org

title: Sec. of War William Eustis to Gen. James Wilkinson, two War Department letters with a ciphered message / part in cypher
shelfmark: Chicago History Museum, James Wilkinson papers, 1764-1823 (bulk 1792-1815), item 91 (4 May 1809, 'receipt of ciphered message') and item 93 (10 May 1809, 'part of message in cypher'), inventory pages 66-67
folio_note: two letters; amount of cipher unknown (item 93 'part of message')
status: CHM finding aid (CARLI chm_fa/2106, PDF) lists both as routine War Department letters with cipher content; no decipherment noted. Wilkinson's other cipher letters (Burr 1806; the Spanish-agent letters, a catalogue entry on AGI Cuba) are already in the repo. Item 116 (12 Dec 1805, 'Truly deciphered, F. Pinckney, Clk.', 'From Burr') is endorsed as deciphered and left out.
why: Cipher traffic between the Secretary of War and Wilkinson just before his recall and court of inquiry, possibly in the same system as the Burr correspondence.
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Chicago Collections Consortium sweep (research/chi_consortium/); not viewed; no images online
verify: Ask the CHM Abakanowicz Research Center for scans of items 91 and 93; check Wilkinson's Memoirs (1816) and the Madison Papers for the same letters printed with the cipher resolved.

title: Wilkinson papers, undated fragment: report of a conversation avowing allegiance to the US rather than Britain, 'contains numerical cypher notations'
shelfmark: Chicago History Museum, James Wilkinson papers, item 174 (no date, no place), vol. 12
status: CHM finding aid description only; numerical cipher notations noted, no decipherment. May belong to the numerical Wilkinson-Spain family (catalogue entry 'Wilkinson (Agent 13)').
why: A numerical-cipher fragment inside the Wilkinson papers could carry part of the dictionary-and-table code used with the Spanish governors, a crib for the unread Papeles de Cuba pages.

title: Pinkerton agency reports on the CB&Q strike: telegrams between G. Godding and 'J.A.B.' said to be in a private cipher
correspondents: Pinkerton operatives to Q. W. Pinkerton, Gen. Supt. W. Division
shelfmark: Newberry Library, Chicago, Burlington and Quincy Railroad Company records, box 106, folder 811 (digital item CBQ_33_1880_09, scan 052_005)
folio_note: the report page says Godding and J.A.B. 'understand each other in having a cipher to use in their telegrams'; the telegrams themselves were not located in the transcription
status: Newberry Transcribe volunteer transcription names a cipher in telegrams between a striker and an agent; no ciphertext seen. Reconnaissance row only; the ciphertext may be in neighbouring folders.
why: Labour spying: a private cipher between a Brotherhood official and a Pinkerton operative in the 1888 Burlington strike; probably a simple code, unexamined.
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Chicago Collections Consortium sweep (research/chi_consortium/); transcription read, scan not viewed
verify: Open the page and its neighbours in box 106 f.811 for the telegrams; if none, drop.
